note: The manicure index for other countries. No country here has a manicure price in money, so every one is tier B: a price index for hairdressing and personal grooming (mostly haircuts) set against that country's own pay, both rebased to 2015 = 100. price_to_pay_index above 100 means the service takes more work to pay for than in 2015. Brazil is the exception inside tier B: its index is for manicures alone (nail_specific: true). Pay is the OECD's mean annual wage for both sexes, except Brazil. The UK and the US also carry women's median pay. Nothing is converted between currencies and price levels are never compared across countries. Series with derived: true are worked out here by the formula in their label. Years with a missing input are left out.
tier_a: None in this file. The only true manicure price found is the UK's, in uk-manicure-prices.json and uk-manicure-affordability.json. The UK entry here repeats its minutes of work under true_manicure for comparison.
